description: Third held-out set of synthetic meetings for the notes variant eval, written without reference to the sidecar code or the earlier held-out sets. Each meeting mixes conditional and negated commitments, date corrections, spoken section labels, product or vendor names that read like people, restricted prices or quantities, non-task questions or suggestions, completed statuses and reported actions. Not used by Rust tests.

segments.speaker: Odile
segments.text: Pricing review. The quote from Fenwick, our billing vendor, is twelve dollars per seat only for registered nonprofits, and the standard rate is nineteen dollars per seat.

segments.speaker: Bram
segments.text: Can I ask whether Fenwick offers an annual discount? It's only a question; I'm not taking it on.

segments.speaker: Talia
segments.text: I'll draft the pricing memo by Thursday, and we agreed to sign the Fenwick order once the board approves the nonprofit tier.

segments.speaker: Odile
segments.text: Small correction for Talia. The memo is due Tuesday, not Thursday.

segments.speaker: Talia
segments.text: Got it, Tuesday.

segments.speaker: Odile
segments.text: Status: the security questionnaire is already done. We haven't approved the five extra admin seats.

segments.speaker: Wren
segments.text: Library planning. Ash Hall can lend us eight rooms except during exams, and the east wing has three rooms all term.

segments.speaker: Dario
segments.text: Then I'll book the three east wing rooms by Tuesday, as long as facilities unlocks the booking portal.

segments.speaker: Sunniva
segments.text: Ingrid from facilities already confirmed the fire inspection. I won't publish the timetable until Dario books the rooms.

segments.speaker: Kofi
segments.text: Furniture: the north floor has forty study carrels, the annex has twelve group tables, and the chair budget is $2,400. I'll order the new chairs by the 9th.

segments.speaker: Wren
segments.text: Furniture: one correction, the supplier is closed that week, so Kofi orders the chairs by the 16th instead.

segments.speaker: Kofi
segments.text: Fine, the 16th.

segments.speaker: Mireille
segments.text: Supplier check-in. Harlan, the mill we use, now charges $27 a sack of flour, and there's a $4 delivery fee only on orders under ten sacks.

segments.speaker: Tobias
segments.text: Clementine, the ordering app, keeps dropping the Saturday orders, so I'll export the order history on Monday.

segments.speaker: Anouk
segments.text: If the export looks clean, I'll move us onto the new order template on June 4.

segments.speaker: Mireille
segments.text: Anouk, the template move has to be June 11, not June 4. Harlan's rep is away that week.

segments.speaker: Anouk
segments.text: Okay, June 11.

segments.speaker: Tobias
segments.text: Can I suggest we try another mill for rye? Not an action for anyone, just something to think about.

segments.speaker: Mireille
segments.text: Noted. Bettina already paid the March invoice, and the oven repair is finished.

segments.speaker: Celeste
segments.text: Rehearsal schedule. The cast has fourteen actors, the crew has six stagehands, and the props budget is $850.

segments.speaker: Ronan
segments.text: We agreed to add a Sunday matinee only if presales pass 200 tickets, and I'll print the programs by Friday.

segments.speaker: Imke
segments.text: Rehearsal schedule, again: I won't lock the lighting cues until Yusuf finishes the set changes.

segments.speaker: Yusuf
segments.text: I'll finish the set changes on Wednesday. Sorry, I mean Thursday, not Wednesday.

segments.speaker: Celeste
segments.text: Can I ask, and this isn't a task for anyone, whether the matinee could use the smaller hall? Also, we haven't approved the fog machine.

segments.speaker: Ronan
segments.text: Imke already booked the piano tuner.

segments.speaker: Marisol
segments.text: Food drive sync. Deliveries: Jasper, our refrigerated van, is already repaired.

segments.speaker: Aksel
segments.text: Good. I'll drive Jasper to the north pantry on Thursday unless the inspection slips.

segments.speaker: Fenna
segments.text: Box pricing: the standard price is five dollars a box, and only school pantries pay three dollars a box.

segments.speaker: Marisol
segments.text: We haven't approved a backup van. I'd propose we revisit that in spring, but nobody needs to act on it now. Oskar already collected the donated pallets.

segments.speaker: Aksel
segments.text: I'll send Fenna the route sheet by the 9th.

segments.speaker: Fenna
segments.text: Deliveries: I need the route sheet by the 8th, not the 9th, Aksel.

segments.speaker: Aksel
segments.text: Okay, the 8th then.

segments.speaker: Zofia
segments.text: Release planning. Rowan, our field-notes app, has 640 beta testers, and the support team has closed 95 bug reports.

segments.speaker: Emeka
segments.text: I'll freeze the code on Wednesday after the translation pass lands, and Lise will write the release notes.

segments.speaker: Lise
segments.text: Fine, I'll write the release notes by the 21st. Can I suggest a short changelog video too? That's only an idea, not an action.

segments.speaker: Emeka
segments.text: Pricing: the Pro tier costs $6 a month, or $4 a month only for verified students.

segments.speaker: Zofia
segments.text: Kenji already signed off on the privacy review. We haven't approved the tablet build yet, so I won't announce the launch until the tablet build is approved.

segments.speaker: Lise
segments.text: Emeka, one correction. The code freeze is Thursday, not Wednesday, because the translation vendor slipped a day.

segments.speaker: Emeka
segments.text: Right, Thursday then.
